question: Why does a backend service need resilience policies like timeouts and retries at all?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki har backend kisi aisi cheez ko call karta hai jo uske control mein nahi hai -- payment gateway, SMS API, email provider, doosri team ki service, network ke paar database. Yeh dependencies teen tarah se fail hoti hain: seedha error de deti hain, hang ho jaati hain (kabhi jawab hi nahi aata), ya slow ho jaati hain. Teeno ka asar hamari service par padta hai.

PLAN.md ka "Why this project" yahi kehta hai, aur saath mein ek important baat: naive fixes situation ko aur kharab karte hain. Timeout nahi lagaya toh har hanging call ek request, ek socket aur memory pakad ke baithi rehti hai -- requests pile up hoti hain aur hamari service bhi slow ho jaati hai, matlab dependency ki problem hamari problem ban jaati hai. Retry lagaya par bina backoff ke, toh jo service already down hai usko hum 3x traffic bhej dete hain -- retry storm.

Isliye resilience-kit ek chhoti library hai jo KISI BHI async call ko wrap karti hai: TimeoutPolicy (har attempt ki deadline), RetryPolicy (backoff + jitter ke saath dobara try), RetryBudget (outage mein retries band), CircuitBreaker (down dependency ko call karna band) aur Bulkhead (ek dependency ke liye kitni calls ek saath). Interview mein main yeh bolta hoon: resilience ka goal dependency ko theek karna nahi hai, goal yeh hai ki dependency ki failure hamari service mein na phaile aur jab dependency wapas aaye toh hum use dobara gira na dein.
why_needed: Distributed system mein partial failure normal hai. Agar har call site apna timeout / retry khud likhe toh har jagah alag bugs honge (koi timeout bhool jaayega, koi bina jitter ke retry karega). Ek tested library ek hi jagah yeh rules rakhti hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki wiring mein fuse hota hai. Ek appliance short ho jaaye toh fuse udta hai aur baaki ghar chalta rehta hai. Fuse appliance ko theek nahi karta, bas failure ko phailne se rokta hai -- resilience policies bhi yahi karti hain.
how_it_works: Har policy ek hi shape wrap karti hai: Operation<T> = (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>. Policy operation ko chalati hai aur uske around protection lagati hai: timeout deadline deta hai aur signal abort karta hai, retry failure par wait karke dobara chalata hai, breaker aur bulkhead decide karte hain ki call jaaye bhi ya nahi. wrap() inhe compose karta hai (recommended order retry -> breaker -> bulkhead -> timeout).
in_this_project: README ke "Use it" section mein ek SMS dependency ke liye ek set of policies banaya gaya hai (module level par, ek baar, har call share karti hai): RetryPolicy maxAttempts 3 + RetryBudget + deadlineMs 8000, CircuitBreaker with isFailure: isRetryableHttp, Bulkhead maxConcurrent 20 maxQueue 50, TimeoutPolicy 2000 ms. Core mein koi runtime dependency nahi hai. README status: 179 tests pass (Windows, Node 20), npm par publish NAHI hai -- repo se copy ya local path dependency ki tarah use hoti hai.
advantages: Dependency ki failure hamari service mein nahi phailti
Ek jagah tested rules, har call site par copy-paste nahi
Recovery ke time dependency ko retry storm se bachata hai
disadvantages: Har policy ek aur config hai jise tune karna padta hai (ms, attempts, thresholds)
Galat config (jaise bahut lamba timeout) protection ka bhram deta hai
common_mistakes: Sirf retry lagana aur timeout bhool jaana
Retry bina backoff / jitter ke
Har request par nayi policy banana (budget / breaker ki state share hi nahi hoti)
follow_up_questions: What is the difference between a dependency that fails and one that hangs?
Why must policies be created once per dependency and not per request?
What does a retry storm look like and how do you stop one?

question: What is the Operation / Policy shape in this library and why does every operation receive an AbortSignal?
answer_hinglish:
Poori library ek hi chhoti si shape par khadi hai. src/types.ts mein:

Operation<T> = (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>

aur Policy ek interface hai jiska ek hi method hai: execute(operation, signal?). Yahan `signal` caller ka apna cancel signal hai (jaise incoming HTTP request close ho gayi), aur operation ko jo signal milta hai woh policy ka diya hua hai.

Signal kyun? Kyunki "ruk jao" bolne ka JavaScript mein standard tareeka AbortSignal hai. fetch(url, { signal }) exactly yahi shape hai, aur bahut saare modern drivers bhi signal lete hain. Agar operation signal ko aage pass karta hai, toh jab timeout hota hai, breaker / caller cancel karta hai, ya client disconnect ho jaata hai -- toh asli kaam (socket, query) bhi band hota hai, sirf hamara wait nahi.

Bina signal ke policy sirf "waiting" band kar sakti thi, kaam nahi. Promise ko JavaScript mein bahar se cancel nahi kar sakte; cancellation cooperative hoti hai -- operation ko khud signal sunna padta hai. Isliye contract mein signal pehle din se hai.

Doosra fayda: yeh shape kisi framework ko nahi jaanti. Wahi Policy Express handler, NestJS service, worker ya script mein chalti hai. wrap() bhi ek Policy hi return karta hai, toh composed stack bhi same interface hai -- caller ko pata hi nahi ki andar 1 policy hai ya 4.
why_needed: Common contract ke bina har policy alag API maangti aur compose nahi ho paati. AbortSignal ke bina timeout ke baad bhi request background mein chalti rehti (socket open, query running).
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein waiter ka order slip. Har order ke saath ek "cancel" ghanti bhi kitchen jaati hai. Customer chala gaya toh ghanti bajti hai aur chef wahi dish banana band kar deta hai -- bas waiter ka intezaar khatam karna kaafi nahi.
how_it_works: Policy.execute(operation, signal?) operation ko call karta hai ek signal ke saath. Jo policy cancel kar sakti hai (TimeoutPolicy) woh apna AbortController banati hai aur uska signal operation ko deti hai, caller ke signal ko usse link karke. Jo policy khud cancel nahi karti (RetryPolicy, CircuitBreaker, Bulkhead) woh caller ka signal aage pass kar deti hai, ya caller ne diya hi nahi toh ek shared `NEVER` signal (src/types.ts mein exported `new AbortController().signal` jo kabhi abort nahi hota). TimeoutPolicy aur Bulkhead `listenable(signal)` se NEVER pehchaan ke us par abort listener NAHI lagate.
in_this_project: src/types.ts mein dono types hain. src/types.ts mein ek hi exported `NEVER` hai (`new AbortController().signal`) aur `listenable()`; retry, breaker, bulkhead aur wrap use import karte hain -- operation ko hamesha ek valid signal milta hai, `undefined` kabhi nahi. Pehle har file ka apna NEVER tha aur timeout / bulkhead us shared signal par listeners lagate the: 11+ concurrent calls par MaxListenersExceededWarning aata tha (interview bank likhte waqt mila, F1, fixed; test "50 concurrent calls without a caller signal: no MaxListenersExceededWarning"). test/wrap.test.ts ka "passes the caller's signal down to the operation" prove karta hai ki caller ka signal hi operation tak pahunchta hai, aur "the caller's abort reaches through every layer" 4 layers (retry, breaker, bulkhead, timeout) ke through abort check karta hai.
advantages: Framework-free: koi bhi async kaam is shape mein aa jaata hai
Cancellation standard API se, custom token nahi
Composition easy: wrap() bhi ek Policy hai
disadvantages: Cancellation tabhi kaam karti hai jab operation signal ko aage pass kare
Purane callback-style drivers ko adapt karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Operation ke andar signal ignore karke fetch(url) call karna
Policy ka signal chhod ke caller ka signal directly fetch ko dena (timeout ka abort nahi pahunchega)
Ye maan lena ki Promise ko bahar se cancel kiya ja sakta hai

Why does the library use a NEVER signal instead of undefined?
How would you adapt a driver that does not accept an AbortSignal?

question: What does TimeoutPolicy do when the time runs out?
answer_hinglish:
TimeoutPolicy({ ms }) operation ko ek deadline deta hai. Time khatam hone par woh DO kaam karta hai, aur dono zaroori hain:

1. Operation ko jo signal diya tha use abort karta hai, reason ek TimeoutError. Toh agar operation well-behaved hai (fetch, signal lene waala DB driver), toh woh asli mein ruk jaata hai -- socket band, query cancel.
2. Usi waqt TimeoutError ke saath reject karta hai, chahe operation signal ignore kare. Caller ko wait nahi karna padta.

Kuch details jo interview mein bolne layak hain. Caller ka apna signal link hota hai: caller abort kare toh operation ka signal caller ke reason se abort hota hai aur execute() caller ke reason se reject karta hai. Caller ka signal pehle se aborted hai toh operation call hi nahi hota (signal?.throwIfAborted()). Timer aur caller ke signal par laga listener `finally` mein hamesha hat jaate hain -- tests check karte hain ki koi timer bacha nahi aur listener leak nahi hua. Constructor ms <= 0, NaN ya Infinity ko RangeError se reject karta hai.

Aur ek "late answer" ka case: agar operation timeout ke baad resolve ho jaaye, toh kuch nahi badalta -- caller ko TimeoutError hi mila. Promise.race pehla result le leta hai.

Timeout per attempt hota hai jab woh retry ke andar ho (recommended order mein innermost). Total time ke liye RetryPolicy ka deadlineMs hai, woh alag cheez hai.
why_needed: Timeout ke bina ek hanging dependency har request ko hamesha ke liye pakad leti hai. Aur aisa timeout jo sirf wait band kare, background mein kaam chalne deta hai -- resources phir bhi khatam hote hain.
real_world_analogy: Pizza delivery: 30 minute mein nahi aaya toh order cancel. Sirf phone rakh dena (wait band) kaafi nahi; restaurant ko bolna padta hai "mat bhejo" (abort), warna rider phir bhi nikal jaayega.
how_it_works: execute(): signal?.throwIfAborted(); naya AbortController; caller ke signal par onCallerAbort listener ({ once: true }); setTimeout jo timeout event emit karke controller.abort(new TimeoutError(ms)) karta hai; ek `stopped` promise jo controller.signal abort hote hi uske reason se reject hota hai; phir Promise.race([operation(controller.signal), stopped]); finally mein clearTimeout aur removeEventListener.
in_this_project: src/timeout.ts::TimeoutPolicy. src/errors.ts::TimeoutError mein `timeoutMs` field hai aur wahi object abort reason bhi hai, toh operation pehchaan sakta hai ki abort time ki wajah se hua. test/timeout.test.ts (15 tests, README ke hisaab se): "times out: rejects with TimeoutError AND aborts the operation's signal with it", "rejects on timeout even if the operation ignores its signal", "a late answer after the timeout changes nothing", "removes its listener from the caller's signal (no leak across many calls)". Timeout event bhi emit hota hai: { type: "timeout", policy, timeoutMs }.
advantages: Asli kaam bhi rukta hai (agar operation signal sunta hai)
Signal ignore karne waale operation par bhi caller time par free
Koi timer / listener leak nahi
disadvantages: Signal ignore karne waala operation background mein chalta rehta hai (zombie work)
Har call par AbortController + timer + listeners -- benchmark mein yahi sabse mehenga hissa hai
common_mistakes: Timeout ko retry ke bahar lagana (ek deadline saare attempts ke liye)
clearTimeout bhool jaana -- process exit nahi hota / timers jama hote hain
Timeout bahut lamba rakhna (jaise 30 s) jab user 2 s mein chala jaata hai

question: What is a retry policy and what exactly does maxAttempts count in RetryPolicy?
answer_hinglish:
Retry policy failure ke baad operation ko thoda ruk ke dobara chalati hai, kyunki bahut saari failures transient hoti hain -- ek connection reset, ek 503 jab service deploy ho rahi thi, ek 429. Dobara try karne se user ko error nahi dikhta.

RetryPolicy mein maxAttempts PEHLI CALL KO MILA KE count hota hai, default 3. Matlab maxAttempts: 3 = 1 original call + 2 retries. maxAttempts: 1 = koi retry nahi (test "maxAttempts 1 means no retry at all"). Yeh important hai kyunki libraries alag count karti hain -- bench/overhead.mjs mein comment hai ki cockatiel RETRIES count karta hai, isliye wahan maxAttempts: 2 likha hai taaki dono taraf 3 attempts hon. Interview mein yeh off-by-one ka sawaal aksar aata hai.

Loop ka flow simple hai: attempt chalao; success par budget ko batao aur return. Failure par check karo: caller ne abort kiya? -> caller ka reason throw. shouldRetry ne mana kiya? -> give up "not-retryable". Attempts khatam? -> give up "attempts". Budget khaali? -> "budget". Phir backoff delay nikalo, Retry-After dekho, deadline dekho, event emit karo, aur cancellable sleep.

Give up karte waqt LAST error bina badle rethrow hota hai, wrapper nahi -- taaki caller ka existing `catch (e instanceof HttpError)` kaam karta rahe. Kitne attempts hue aur kyun ruke, yeh onGiveUp / give-up event mein jaata hai.

Constructor maxAttempts 0 ya 1.5 ko RangeError se reject karta hai (Number.isSafeInteger check).
why_needed: Transient failures ko user tak pahunchne se rokne ke liye. Par bina limit ke retry ek outage ko aur bada bana deta hai, isliye attempts ki hard limit zaroori hai.
real_world_analogy: Doston ko phone karna: pehli baar busy, do minute ruk ke phir try, phir thoda zyada ruk ke. Teen baar ke baad message chhod dete ho -- poori raat dial nahi karte.
how_it_works: for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) loop. Har iteration se pehle signal?.throwIfAborted(). attempt >= maxAttempts par giveUp("attempts"). Wait ke liye this.backoff.delayMs(attempt, random) -- yahan `attempt` woh attempt hai jo abhi fail hua, toh retry 1 se pehle wait initialMs hota hai.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts::RetryPolicy, option `maxAttempts?: number; // including the first call; default 3`. test/retry.test.ts: "fail, fail, succeed: 3 calls, waits 100 and 200, an event per retry", "out of attempts: rethrows the LAST error unchanged (same object, not a wrapper)", "maxAttempts 1 means no retry at all". Mutation R18 ("one attempt too many") final code par 7 tests fail karta hai (README, final run).
advantages: Transient errors user tak nahi pahunchte
Hard limit: attempts kabhi unbounded nahi
Give-up reason observable (onGiveUp / give-up event)
disadvantages: Har retry dependency par extra load hai
Latency badhti hai (attempts + waits)
common_mistakes: maxAttempts ko 'retries' samajhna (off by one)
Non-idempotent call (payment) ko bina idempotency key retry karna
Har layer par 3 retries -- 3 x 3 x 3 = 27x amplification

Which errors should never be retried?

question: What is exponential backoff and how is the wait calculated in this library?
answer_hinglish:
Exponential backoff ka matlab: har retry se pehle wait badhta jaata hai, multiply hota hua. Pehla retry jaldi, phir double, phir double -- ek cap tak. Isse dependency ko recover karne ka time milta hai aur hum use lagaatar hit nahi karte.

src/backoff.ts mein formula: retry number n se pehle ka wait = min(maxMs, initialMs x multiplier^(n-1)). Defaults: initialMs 100, multiplier 2, maxMs 10 000 (10 s), jitter "full". Toh jitter "none" ke saath waits 100, 200, 400, 800, ... aur 10 000 par ruk jaata hai. Test "none: initial x multiplier^(n-1), capped at maxMs" initialMs 100, maxMs 1000 ke saath [100, 200, 400, 800, 1000, 1000] expect karta hai.

Ek chhoti si careful baat: multiplier^n bade n par Infinity ho jaata hai. Code Math.min pehle lagata hai -- min(maxMs, Infinity) phir bhi maxMs hai -- toh retry 50 par bhi koi overflow nahi (test "is the default: full jitter, 100 ms, x2, 10 s cap" delayMs(50, high) = 9999 check karta hai). Result Math.floor se integer ms hota hai.

Options validate hote hain: initialMs < 0, maxMs < initialMs, multiplier < 1, ya anjaana jitter -> RangeError. multiplier >= 1 ka matlab hai wait kabhi ghat-ta nahi.

Jitter (none / full / equal) iske upar lagta hai -- woh alag sawaal hai. Aur RetryPolicy custom Backoff object bhi le sakti hai: koi bhi object jiske paas delayMs(n, random) ho.
why_needed: Fixed chhota wait ek down service ko lagaatar hit karta hai; fixed bada wait chhoti blip par bhi user ko der tak rokta hai. Exponential dono ke beech balance hai: blip jaldi theek, lambi outage par pressure kam.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka darwaza khatkhatana: pehli baar jawab nahi aaya toh 1 second ruko, phir 2, phir 4. Har baar zyada sabr, par ek limit ke baad aur zyada nahi rukte.
how_it_works: exponentialBackoff(options) ek Backoff object return karta hai jiska delayMs(retryNumber, random) hai. ceiling = Math.min(maxMs, initialMs * multiplier ** (retryNumber - 1)); phir jitter switch: none -> floor(ceiling), full -> floor(random() * ceiling), equal -> floor(ceiling/2 + random() * ceiling/2). RetryPolicy constructor mein: backoff option mein "delayMs" hai toh custom object, warna exponentialBackoff(options).
in_this_project: src/backoff.ts::exponentialBackoff aur Backoff interface. test/backoff.test.ts (9 tests): values, defaults, retry 50 par cap, 10 000 random draws range mein aur integer, invalid options. Mutations: R9 "backoff exponent off by one" (final code par 13 tests fail), R10 "backoff not capped" (3 tests). Ye numbers README ke Mutation checks section se hain.
advantages: Chhoti blip jaldi recover, lambi outage par kam pressure
Cap se wait unbounded nahi hota
Pure function: test karna aasaan
disadvantages: Jitter ke bina saare clients ek saath wapas aate hain
Lamba cap user latency badha sakta hai
common_mistakes: Cap na lagana (retry 20 par ghanton ka wait)
Exponent off-by-one (pehla wait 200 instead of 100)
Overflow handle na karna (Infinity / NaN delay)

question: What is jitter, and what problem does it solve that plain exponential backoff does not?
answer_hinglish:
Jitter matlab wait mein randomness. Problem "thundering herd" hai: maan lo 1000 clients ek hi second par fail hue (dependency 2 second ke liye gir gayi). Plain exponential backoff ke saath sab exactly 100 ms baad retry karenge, phir sab exactly 200 ms baad. Load spread nahi hua, bas shift hua -- har retry wave ek naya spike hai jo recover hoti hui service ko phir gira sakta hai.

Jitter har client ka wait thoda alag kar deta hai, toh retries time mein phail jaate hain. src/backoff.ts mein teen modes hain, ceiling = min(maxMs, initialMs x multiplier^(n-1)):

- none: exactly ceiling. Deterministic. Ek client ke liye theek, fleet ke liye thundering herd (README ke words).
- full (default): random in [0, ceiling). Sabse zyada spread.
- equal: ceiling/2 + random in [0, ceiling/2). Spread kam, par kabhi lagbhag-turant retry nahi hota.

Full jitter default kyun -- PLAN.md AWS ke "Exponential Backoff And Jitter" recommendation ko cite karta hai: jo clients saath fail hue unhe saath wapas nahi aana chahiye. Full jitter ki ek side effect: kabhi kabhi wait 0 ke paas hota hai, toh ek retry turant ho sakta hai. Yahi trade-off equal jitter fix karta hai.

Ek implementation detail: random function inject hoti hai (RetryOptions.random, default Math.random), isliye tests deterministic hain -- jaise random () => 0.5 ke saath default policy ke waits [50, 100] hote hain.
why_needed: Retry ka poora point dependency ko recover hone dena hai. Synchronized retries recovery ke exact moment par spike bhejte hain -- jitter ke bina backoff aadha kaam karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Cinema ka show khatam hua aur sab ek saath parking exit par -- jam. Agar log 0-10 minute random ruk ke niklein toh exit smoothly chalta hai. Jitter wahi random ruk-na hai.
how_it_works: delayMs(n, random) ceiling nikalta hai, phir jitter ke hisaab se: none -> floor(ceiling); full -> floor(random() * ceiling); equal -> floor(ceiling / 2 + random() * (ceiling / 2)). random() [0, 1) deta hai toh full ka result [0, ceiling) mein aur equal ka [ceiling/2, ceiling) mein rehta hai.
in_this_project: src/backoff.ts::Jitter type = "none" | "full" | "equal". test/backoff.test.ts: "full: between 0 and the exponential value" (n=3: low -> 0, high -> 399, 0.5 -> 200), "equal: between half and the whole exponential value" (low -> 200, high -> 399), aur 10 000 random draws (40 retry numbers x 250) jo range mein aur integer rehte hain. test/retry.test.ts "uses the default full jitter with the injected random": waits [50, 100]. Mutations R11 "full jitter missing" aur R12 "equal jitter is full jitter" (R12 sirf 1 test pakadta hai, README).
advantages: Synchronized retry waves tootti hain
Recover hoti service par load smooth
Injected random se deterministic tests
disadvantages: Individual call ka latency unpredictable
Full jitter kabhi ~0 ms wait deta hai
common_mistakes: Fleet mein jitter 'none' rakhna
Jitter ko sirf +/- 10% chhota noise samajhna (spread kaafi nahi)
Tests mein Math.random directly use karna (flaky tests)

question: What is the HTTP Retry-After header and how does parseRetryAfter read it?
answer_hinglish:
Retry-After ek response header hai jisme server khud batata hai ki dobara kab aana -- usually 429 (Too Many Requests) ya 503 (Service Unavailable) ke saath. Iske do valid forms hain:

1. delay-seconds: "120" matlab 120 second baad.
2. HTTP-date: "Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT" matlab us time ke baad.

src/http.ts::parseRetryAfter(header, nowMs = Date.now()) dono padhta hai aur milliseconds return karta hai, ya undefined agar header missing / samajh nahi aaya:

- null / undefined -> undefined.
- trim ke baad sirf digits (/^\d+$/) -> Number(value) x 1000. Toh "120" -> 120 000, "0" -> 0, " 5 " -> 5000.
- agar value mein ek bhi letter nahi hai -> undefined. Yeh "-5", "1.5", "" ko reject karta hai, jo valid header nahi hain (Date.parse inhe kabhi kabhi date samajh leta).
- warna Date.parse; NaN -> undefined; date past mein hai -> 0 ("now"), Math.max(0, at - nowMs).

Interview point: seconds ko ms samajh lena common bug hai -- mutation R29 "Retry-After seconds read as ms" yahi tha (3 tests ne pakda). R30 (past date ka negative delay) aur R31 ("-5" aur "1.5" date maan lena) bhi tests ne pakde.

Header parse karna aadha kaam hai; RetryPolicy use kaise karti hai (longer than backoff ho tabhi, maxRetryAfterMs se zyada toh give up) -- woh alag concept hai. HttpError(status, retryAfterMs) mein parsed value carry hoti hai.
why_needed: Server jab khud bata raha hai ki kab aana, toh usse pehle aana sirf ek aur 429 kamaana hai. Header sahi padhne se hum server ki rate limit respect karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ke shutter par board: "lunch, 2 baje khulega". Woh ya toh "30 minute mein" likhta hai ya "2:00 PM". Dono samajhne padte hain, aur 1:45 par khatkhatane ka fayda nahi.
how_it_works: Regex check order matter karta hai: pehle pure integer (seconds), phir "letter hai ya nahi" guard, phir Date.parse. nowMs parameter inject hota hai taaki date waale cases deterministic test ho sakein.
in_this_project: src/http.ts::parseRetryAfter. test/http.test.ts mein cases: "120" -> 120 000, "0" -> 0, " 5 " -> 5000, "Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:00:30 GMT" -> 30 000 (fixed now ke saath), past date -> 0; aur null, undefined, "", "-5", "1.5", "soon" -> undefined; aur ek 400-digit value -> Infinity (RetryPolicy phir give up karti hai). Real server test "429 with Retry-After: 1 -> the policy waits the 1000 ms the server asked for".

Garbage par undefined, crash nahi
nowMs inject hone se testable
disadvantages: Date form client aur server ki clock skew par depend karta hai
Date.parse lenient hai; letter guard ek heuristic hai
common_mistakes: Seconds ko ms samajhna
Past date par negative delay
Sirf seconds form support karna

question: Why does TimeoutPolicy abort the operation's signal instead of only stopping the wait?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki ek timeout jo sirf WAITING band karta hai, asli kaam ko chalne deta hai. Promise.race(op, timer) se caller ko time par error mil jaata hai, par fetch ka socket open rehta hai, DB query execute hoti rehti hai, dependency par load bana rehta hai. Har timeout ek "zombie" request chhod jaata hai. Ek slow dependency ke against yeh khatarnaak hai: hum timeout karte jaate hain, naye requests bhejte jaate hain, aur purane abhi bhi chal rahe hain -- connections aur dependency dono par load double hota jaata hai.

PLAN.md ka decision exactly yahi hai: "A timeout that only stops WAITING leaves the request running (socket open, query still executing)." Isliye TimeoutPolicy ek AbortController banata hai, uska signal operation ko deta hai, aur timeout par controller.abort(new TimeoutError(ms)) karta hai. Operation fetch(url, { signal }) karta hai toh fetch connection band kar deta hai.

Yeh dava sirf claim nahi, test hai. test/http.test.ts mein ek real node:http server loopback par chalta hai jo kabhi jawab nahi deta (hang handler), aur server count karta hai ki kitni responses `writableFinished` se pehle close huin. Test "a server that hangs: TimeoutError, and the request is really cancelled (the server sees the connection close)" 200 ms timeout ke baad expect karta hai ki server ne closed() = 1 dekha. Matlab server side par connection sach mein tootta hai.

Abort reason bhi TimeoutError hi hai (wahi object jo reject hota hai), toh operation pehchaan sakta hai ki cancel time ki wajah se hua -- mutation R1 ("timeout aborts without the TimeoutError reason") ko tests pakadte hain.
why_needed: Timeouts ka maqsad resources free karna hai. Agar resources (socket, query, dependency ka CPU) free nahi hote, toh timeout sirf error message jaldi deta hai, protection nahi.
real_world_analogy: Online order cancel karna aur sirf app band kar dena -- app band karne se delivery nahi rukti, rider phir bhi aayega. Cancel button dabana (abort) zaroori hai.
how_it_works: AbortController.abort(reason) controller.signal par "abort" event fire karta hai. fetch us event ko sunta hai aur underlying request ko tod deta hai, AbortError / reason ke saath reject karke. question: How is the caller's own AbortSignal linked into TimeoutPolicy, and what does 'cooperative cancellation' mean here?
answer_hinglish:
TimeoutPolicy do signals handle karta hai: caller ka signal (jaise client ne connection band kiya) aur apna internal AbortController. Caller ka signal internal controller se link hota hai: caller ke signal par ek `onCallerAbort` listener lagta hai ({ once: true }) jo controller.abort(signal.reason) karta hai. Toh caller abort kare toh (1) operation ka signal caller ke REASON se abort hota hai aur (2) execute() turant usi reason se reject hota hai, kyunki `stopped` promise controller ke abort par reject hota hai. Caller ka signal pehle se aborted ho toh signal?.throwIfAborted() operation call hi nahi karta. Aur finally mein listener hata diya jaata hai -- warna ek long-lived signal par har call ek listener chhod jaati (test "removes its listener from the caller's signal (no leak across many calls)", 5 calls par added = removed).

Cooperative cancellation ka matlab: JavaScript mein kisi chalte Promise ko bahar se maarne ka koi tareeka nahi. Hum sirf signal abort karke "please ruk jao" bol sakte hain; operation ko khud signal padhna ya fetch / driver ko pass karna padta hai. Isliye TimeoutPolicy dual design karta hai: signal abort (cooperative part) + race se turant reject (non-cooperative safety net). Agar operation signal ignore kare, toh caller time par free ho jaata hai (test "rejects on timeout even if the operation ignores its signal"), PAR operation ka kaam background mein chalta rehta hai -- yeh library ki limitation nahi, JavaScript ka model hai, aur README "Use it" mein clearly likha hai: signal aage pass karo.
why_needed: Ek client jo chala gaya uske liye kaam karte rehna pure waste hai. PLAN.md: "A client that went away should stop the work, the retries and the backoff wait at once."
real_world_analogy: Referee whistle bajata hai -- khiladi ruk jaate hain kyunki woh rules maante hain. Referee unhe pakad ke rok nahi sakta. Jo khiladi whistle ignore kare, uska goal count nahi hota (race reject), par woh daudta rehta hai.

Node 20 ka AbortSignal.any() bhi yeh kar sakta tha, par yahan manual listener hai aur cleanup explicit hai.

question: Which errors are worth retrying, and how does isRetryableHttp decide?
answer_hinglish:
Rule simple hai: woh error retry karo jo dobara try karne par BADAL sakta hai. Jo error same request par same jawab dega, use retry karna sirf load badhaata hai.

src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp(error):
- BrokenCircuitError ya BulkheadRejectedError -> false. Inka poora point fail fast hai; turant retry phir wahi open breaker / full bulkhead hit karega.
- HttpError NAHI hai (network error jaise "fetch failed" TypeError, ya TimeoutError) -> true. Koi jawab hi nahi mila, toh dobara try reasonable hai.
- HttpError hai: retryable sirf 408 (Request Timeout), 429 (Too Many Requests) aur 5xx MINUS 501 (Not Implemented -- method kabhi implement nahi hoga, retry bekaar).
- Baaki 4xx (400, 401, 403, 404, 422) -> false: request hi galat hai, dobara bhejne se nahi sudhregi.

Yeh function do jagah kaam aata hai. RetryPolicy ka shouldRetry (README example), aur CircuitBreaker ka isFailure -- kyunki 404 service ka sahi jawab hai, "down" hone ka sign nahi; test "404s do not open a breaker that uses isRetryableHttp as isFailure".

Ek design detail: HttpError ka field `upstreamStatus` hai, `status` nahi. Express ka default error handler err.status client ko bhej deta hai, toh `status` se dependency ka 401 HAMARE client ko "unauthorized" bata deta. Yeh Express test ne pakda tha, stage 3 mein rename hua.

Ek caveat jo main interview mein zaroor bolta: "retryable" ka matlab "safe to retry" nahi hai. Network error ya timeout ke baad non-idempotent POST (payment) server par shayad ho chuka ho -- isRetryableHttp idempotency nahi jaanta.
why_needed: Galat errors retry karna dependency par bekaar load aur user ko lamba wait deta hai; sahi errors retry na karna transient blips ko user errors bana deta hai.
real_world_analogy: ATM se paise nahi nikle: "network error" -- dobara try karo. "Insufficient balance" -- dobara try karne se balance nahi badlega.
how_it_works: Order of checks matter karta hai: pehle resilience rejections (false), phir non-HTTP (true), phir status code ranges. `s === 408 || s === 429 || (s >= 500 && s !== 501)`.

Real server tests: "404 is not retried" (1 hit), "503, 503, 200: the third request succeeds". Mutations: R27 "every 4xx retried" (8 tests), R28 "501 retried" (1), K9 "breaker / bulkhead rejections retried".

4xx par bekaar load nahi
Fail-fast rejections retry loop mein nahi phanste
disadvantages: Idempotency ka koi idea nahi

question: How does shouldRetry work in RetryPolicy, and why does a non-retryable error not touch the retry budget?
answer_hinglish:
shouldRetry(error, attempt) => boolean ek predicate hai jo RetryPolicy har failure par poochti hai: "kya yeh error dobara try karne layak hai?". Default: option na diya toh HAR error retry hota hai. README aur code comment dono kehte hain ki real use mein un errors ko "no" bolo jo nahi badlenge (400, 401, 403, 404, 422, validation errors). HTTP ke liye ready-made isRetryableHttp hai.

attempt argument bhi milta hai (1 = pehli call), toh predicate attempt par depend kar sakta hai -- jaise ek error ko sirf pehli baar retry karna. Test "shouldRetry sees the attempt number" maxAttempts 5 ke saath predicate attempt < 2 deta hai: seen [1, 2], aur error "fail 2" rethrow hota hai.

shouldRetry false de toh give up reason "not-retryable" hai aur original error rethrow hota hai, ek hi call ke baad.

Budget waali baat: code mein order dekho -- shouldRetry check PEHLE hai, budget.onFailure() BAAD mein. Toh non-retryable error budget ka token nahi khaata. Reason PLAN.md mein: ek 404 dependency ki health ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta. Agar 404s budget drain karein toh ek client jo galat IDs maang raha hai, baaki sab ke genuine 503 retries band karwa dega. Test "a non-retryable error is rethrown after one call and does not touch the budget" -- budget.available 10 hi rehta hai. Mutation R17 ("non-retryable errors drain the budget") exactly ek test pakadta hai.

Ek aur rule jo shouldRetry se bhi upar hai: caller ne abort kar diya ho toh failure kabhi retry nahi hota, aur woh bhi budget ko nahi chhoota -- catch block ki pehli line hai.
why_needed: Har error same nahi hai. Ek predicate se caller apni domain knowledge (kaunse codes transient hain) policy mein daal sakta hai bina RetryPolicy badle.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ke paas: bukhaar -- do din baad phir dikhao. Toota haath -- "do din baad phir try" se nahi judega, alag treatment chahiye.
how_it_works: catch block ka order: (1) signal?.aborted -> throw signal.reason; (2) shouldRetry false -> giveUp("not-retryable"); (3) budget?.onFailure(); (4) attempt >= maxAttempts -> giveUp("attempts"); (5) budget canRetry false -> giveUp("budget"); phir delay. giveUp onGiveUp callback (quietly, throw contained) aur give-up event dono chalata hai aur original error throw karta hai.

404s shared budget nahi kha sakte
attempt-aware decisions possible
disadvantages: Default 'retry everything' galat use mein 4xx bhi retry karta hai
Predicate galat likha toh silently bekaar retries

Budget ko har error par charge karna
Predicate mein side effects (logging ke alawa) daalna

question: How does RetryPolicy combine Retry-After with its own backoff, and when does it give up instead of waiting?
answer_hinglish:
Teen rules hain, aur teeno ka ek hi principle hai: server ne jitna wait bola usse PEHLE kabhi retry mat karo, par request ko ghanton park bhi mat karo.

1. retryAfterMs(error) option ek function hai jo error se server ka maanga hua delay nikalta hai (README: e instanceof HttpError ? e.retryAfterMs : undefined). Policy pehle apna backoff delay nikalti hai, phir asked dekhti hai. Agar asked NaN nahi hai aur backoff se BADA hai, toh asked use hota hai (Math.ceil). Chhota hai toh backoff hi rehta hai -- jo already asked se lamba hai. Dono case mein final delay >= asked. Test "Retry-After longer than the backoff is honoured; shorter is ignored": asked [5000, 10], backoff 100 / 200 -> sleeps [5000, 200].

2. Agar asked > maxRetryAfterMs (default 60 000 ms) -> give up, reason "retry-after-too-long", original error rethrow, koi sleep nahi. Code comment: "Retry-After: 3600" ke liye request park karna galat hai, aur EARLIER retry karna sirf ek aur 429 kamaayega. Toh do hi honest options hain: wait karo ya chhod do; policy chhodti hai.

3. Iske baad deadline check hota hai -- toh agar asked delay deadlineMs ke baahar le jaata hai, toh bhi give up ("deadline").

Real HTTP test: server 429 + "retry-after: 1" bhejta hai, aur injected sleep record karta hai [1000] -- backoff (1-5 ms) nahi, server ka 1000 ms.

Mutations jo yahan bane: R21 (Retry-After ignored), R22 (cap ignored), R32 (chhota Retry-After backoff ko override kare) -- sab caught.

Ek edge case: ek 400-digit "Retry-After" parseRetryAfter mein Infinity ban jaata hai. Check `!Number.isNaN(asked)` hai, isFinite nahi -- toh Infinity "too long" gina jaata hai aur give up hota hai; sirf NaN ignore hota hai (normal backoff). Test: "an absurdly long Retry-After (Infinity, e.g. 400 digits) gives up too; NaN is ignored".
why_needed: 429 / 503 ke saath Retry-After server ka explicit backpressure signal hai. Ise ignore karna rate limiter se ladna hai; blindly maanna kabhi request ko minutes tak latka deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank token system: "aapka number 20 minute baad". 2 minute baad jaake poochoge toh phir wahi jawab. Aur agar bole "kal aana" -- toh line mein baithe nahi rehte, ghar jaate ho aur user ko bata dete ho.
how_it_works: let delayMs = backoff.delayMs(attempt, random); const asked = o.retryAfterMs?.(error); if (asked !== undefined && !Number.isNaN(asked) && asked > delayMs) { if (asked > (o.maxRetryAfterMs ?? 60_000)) giveUp("retry-after-too-long"); delayMs = Math.ceil(asked); } -- phir deadline check, phir onRetry / retry event (delayMs final value ke saath), phir sleep.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts::RetryPolicy options retryAfterMs aur maxRetryAfterMs. test/retry.test.ts: "Retry-After longer than the backoff is honoured; shorter is ignored", "Retry-After longer than maxRetryAfterMs: gives up instead of waiting" (3 600 000 vs 60 000, sleeps [] aur reason retry-after-too-long). test/http.test.ts: "429 with Retry-After: 1 -> the policy waits the 1000 ms the server asked for".

Kabhi asked se pehle retry nahi
Lamba wait par fast give-up, request park nahi
disadvantages: Retry-After deadline se bada ho toh request fail -- user ko error
Fleet mein sab clients same Retry-After maanein toh woh bhi ek synchronized wave hai (asked delay par jitter nahi lagta)
common_mistakes: Backoff aur Retry-After mein se hamesha Retry-After lena (chhota bhi)
Cap na rakhna
Seconds ko ms padhna

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Wait vs give up ka trade-off hai. 60 s default ek middle ground hai: background job ke liye kam ho sakta hai, user-facing request ke liye bahut zyada. Isliye maxRetryAfterMs option hai aur deadlineMs bhi -- user request mein deadline pehle trigger hogi. Retry-After par jitter nahi lagta (delayMs = Math.ceil(asked)), jo "kabhi pehle mat aao" guarantee ko simple rakhta hai par saare clients ko same moment par bhej sakta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Server galat Retry-After bheje (bahut bada) -> har call turant give up, user ko errors. Server HTTP-date bheje aur clocks skewed hon -> delay galat. Retry-After maanne ke baad bhi 429 aaye -> agla attempt / give up, budget token kharch.
advanced.alternatives: Retry-After par upar se thoda jitter (jaise asked + random 0-10%); ya 429 ko RetryPolicy mein retry karne ke bajaye client-side rate limiter / queue mein daalna; ya background jobs ke liye request ko job queue mein reschedule karna (park in a queue, not in memory).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x clients ek rate-limited API par: sab ek hi Retry-After value maanenge aur ek saath wapas aayenge. Wahan per-client token bucket ya central queue better hai. Is library mein kuch bhi process ke bahar share nahi hota -- har replica khud seekhta hai (README NOT implemented).
advanced.production_improvements: give-up event ke reason par metric (retry-after-too-long count) taaki pata chale dependency kitni baar lambi waits maang raha hai; maxRetryAfterMs ko per-dependency tune karna; API response mein apna Retry-After forward karna jab upstream ne maanga ho (abhi adapter yeh nahi karta, sirf breaker / bulkhead par Retry-After deta hai).

question: What is the difference between RetryPolicy's deadlineMs and a TimeoutPolicy?
answer_hinglish:
Dono time limit hain, par alag cheez ko limit karte hain.

TimeoutPolicy ek ATTEMPT ki limit hai. Recommended order (retry -> breaker -> bulkhead -> timeout) mein woh innermost hai, toh har attempt ko apna fresh timer milta hai, aur time khatam hone par woh operation ka signal abort karta hai.

deadlineMs RetryPolicy ka option hai: saare attempts aur unke beech ke waits ka TOTAL budget. Code comment: "total time for all attempts and waits; a retry that would start after it is not made". Matlab yeh kisi chalte attempt ko abort NAHI karta. Yeh sirf retry se pehle decide karta hai: agar (now + delayMs - startedAt) >= deadlineMs, toh give up with reason "deadline" aur last error rethrow. Test: deadline 1000, waits 100, 200, 400 (t = 700), agla wait 800 -> 1500 >= 1000, toh give up; error "fail 4".

Toh deadline "agla retry START mat karo" hai, timeout "yeh attempt ab band karo" hai. Isliye dono saath chahiye: timeout per attempt (2000 ms) + deadline total (8000 ms), jaise README example mein. Deadline ke bina 3 attempts x 2 s timeout + backoff waits user ko 6+ s rok sakte hain; timeout ke bina ek hanging attempt deadline ko kabhi check hone hi nahi dega (check sirf failure ke baad hota hai).

Kya hota agar timeout ko retry ke BAHAR lagaya? test/wrap.test.ts dikhata hai: ek deadline saare attempts aur waits ke liye, aur 150 ms timeout doosre wait ke beech fire ho jaata hai -- teesra attempt kabhi nahi hota. Yeh deadline jaisa lagta hai, par yeh chalte kaam ko beech mein kaat deta hai; deadlineMs wahi kaam saaf tareeke se karta hai.
why_needed: User ka patience total time ka hota hai, attempt ka nahi. Per-attempt timeout akela total latency bound nahi karta; deadline akela hanging attempt nahi todta.
real_world_analogy: Exam mein har sawaal ke liye 10 minute (timeout) aur poore paper ke liye 3 ghante (deadline). 3 ghante khatam hone wale hain toh naya sawaal shuru nahi karte -- par jo likh rahe ho woh beech mein nahi chheena jaata.
how_it_works: startedAt = now() execute ki shuruaat mein. Har failure par delay nikalne ke baad: if (o.deadlineMs !== undefined && now() + delayMs - startedAt >= o.deadlineMs) giveUp("deadline"). now inject hota hai (test hook). Constructor deadlineMs <= 0 ya non-finite ko RangeError deta hai.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts option deadlineMs. test/retry.test.ts "deadline: no retry that would start after it" -- injected now aur sleep jo t ko aage badhata hai, koi real wait nahi. test/wrap.test.ts: "timeout INSIDE retry: every attempt gets its own deadline (hang, hang, ok -> ok)" aur "timeout OUTSIDE retry: one deadline for all attempts and waits (the third attempt never happens)". Mutation R23 "deadline ignored" ek hi test pakadta hai.

Chalte attempt ko beech mein nahi kaat-ta
Wasteful last retry jo time par khatam hi nahi hoga, shuru hi nahi hota
disadvantages: Hard bound nahi: aakhri attempt deadline ke baad tak chal sakta hai (uski limit timeout hai)
Deadline downstream services ko propagate nahi hoti -- yeh implement nahi hai
common_mistakes: Sirf timeout ko retry ke bahar lagake 'deadline' maan lena

question: Why does RetryPolicy rethrow the last error unchanged instead of a RetriesExhaustedError wrapper?
answer_hinglish:
Decision PLAN.md mein likha hai: "Retry rethrows the last error unchanged. Callers keep their existing error handling (instanceof HttpError); attempts and the reason go to onGiveUp. Chosen over a RetriesExhaustedError wrapper, which forces every caller to unwrap."

Socho ek existing codebase jisme already `catch (e) { if (e instanceof HttpError && e.upstreamStatus === 404) ... }` hai. Agar hum retry add karte hain aur woh RetriesExhaustedError { cause } throw karta hai, toh yeh saara code chupchaap toot jaata hai -- instanceof false, 404 handling band, sab generic 500 ban jaata hai. Retry add karna ek "transparent" change hona chahiye; caller ko wahi error milna chahiye jo bina retry ke milta, bas kam baar.

Wrapper ka fayda yeh hota ki caller ko pata chale kitne attempts hue aur kyun ruke. Woh information yahan side channel mein jaati hai: onGiveUp({ attempts, reason, error }) aur ek give-up event { type: "give-up", policy, attempts, reason, error }. Reasons: attempts, not-retryable, budget, deadline, retry-after-too-long. Logs / metrics ke liye yeh kaafi hai, aur caller ka control flow saaf rehta hai.

"LAST" error kyun, pehla nahi? Last error dependency ki current state batata hai -- jaise pehla 503 tha, aakhri 429 with Retry-After -- aur same object hota hai (test expect(e).toBe(f.errors[2])), copy nahi, toh stack trace aur fields intact.

Yeh sabse zyada tests waala rule hai: mutation R25 ("gives up with a wrapper instead of the last error") final code par 20 tests fail karta hai (README, final run). Matlab poori test suite is contract par tiki hai.
why_needed: Resilience layer ko caller ke code se invisible hona chahiye. Error type badalna ek breaking API change hai jo har call site ko chhoota hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier teen baar deliver karne ki koshish karta hai, phir parcel wapas "address not found" ke saath. Woh aapko naya label "3 attempts failed (andar dekho)" nahi deta -- asli wajah wahi rehti hai, attempts ka record tracking page (logs) par hai.
how_it_works: giveUp(reason) closure: o.onGiveUp?.({ attempts: attempt, reason, error }); emit(o.onEvent, { type: "give-up", ... }); throw error; -- `error` wahi catch variable hai jo last attempt ne throw kiya. Caller abort par alag path: throw signal.reason (caller ka reason, kyunki caller ne hi cancel kiya).
in_this_project: src/retry.ts::RetryPolicy, GiveUpEvent, GiveUpReason. test/retry.test.ts "out of attempts: rethrows the LAST error unchanged (same object, not a wrapper)". test/http.test.ts "all attempts 503: the last HttpError comes back unchanged" (rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "HttpError", upstreamStatus: 503 })). Events system (src/events.ts) give-up event deta hai; handler throw kare toh ignore hota hai.

instanceof / field checks kaam karte rehte hain
Attempts / reason phir bhi observable (events)
disadvantages: Caller ko catch block mein pata nahi ki retries hue
Pehle attempts ke errors kho jaate hain (sirf events mein dikhte hain)
common_mistakes: Wrapper throw karna aur caller ka instanceof todna
Last error ki jagah pehla error throw karna
Error ko naye Error(msg) mein copy karna (stack aur fields kho jaate)

Yahan context events mein gaya. Downside: caller jo per-request decision lena chahe (jaise "retries ke baad fail hua toh fallback") use events se correlate karna padega.

question: Why is full jitter the default, and when would you choose equal jitter or no jitter instead?
answer_hinglish:
Full jitter default hai kyunki library ka main scenario ek fleet hai: bahut saare processes / requests jo EK SAATH fail hote hain (dependency ek second ke liye giri). PLAN.md: "Full jitter by default (the AWS 'Exponential Backoff And Jitter' recommendation): many clients that failed together must not come back together." Full jitter [0, ceiling) mein uniform random deta hai -- spread sabse zyada, isliye recovery ke moment par synchronized spike sabse kam.

Equal jitter: ceiling/2 + random [0, ceiling/2). Spread aadha, par minimum wait ceiling ka aadha hai -- "never retries almost at once" (README). Kab use karoon: jab dependency ko ek minimum saans chahiye (jaise woh restart ho rahi hai aur turant retry pakka fail hoga), ya jab ek client ke liye wait ka lower bound chahiye.

None: exactly ceiling. Deterministic. README: "fine for one client, a thundering herd for a fleet". Kab: ek single batch job / CLI script, jahan predictability debugging ke liye zyada kaam ki hai; aur tests mein (test/retry.test.ts ka recorder jitter "none" use karta hai taaki waits [100, 200] exact hon).

Full jitter ka cost: ek call ka wait kabhi 0 ke paas -- matlab effectively immediate retry, aur expected wait ceiling/2 hai, toh exponential "pressure" kam lagta hai individual client ke liye. Par aggregate load (fleet) ke liye wahi best hai, jo yahan matter karta hai.

Honesty point: library mein decorrelated jitter (AWS ka teesra variant) built-in nahi hai -- par Backoff interface custom object leta hai, toh koi bhi apna strategy daal sakta hai.
why_needed: Default woh hona chahiye jo galat use par sabse kam nuksaan kare. Fleet mein jitter none outage ko lamba kar sakta hai; full jitter ka worst case ek-do jaldi retries hain.
real_world_analogy: School chhutti ke baad gate: full jitter = bachche 0-10 minute mein kabhi bhi niklein (sabse kam bheed); equal = 5-10 minute ke beech (thoda bheed, par koi turant nahi); none = sab ek ghanti par (stampede).
how_it_works: Teeno same ceiling use karte hain; fark sirf random component ka range hai. full: floor(random() * ceiling); equal: floor(ceiling / 2 + random() * (ceiling / 2)); none: floor(ceiling).
in_this_project: src/backoff.ts::exponentialBackoff default jitter "full". test/backoff.test.ts har mode ke boundary values check karta hai. R12 ("equal jitter is full jitter") sirf ek test pakadta hai -- README ki list mein woh breaks hain jo exactly ek test se pakde gaye, matlab woh test delete hua toh bug chhup jaayega.

new RetryPolicy({ backoff: { jitter: "full" } });   // API -> shared dependency, many replicas (default)
new RetryPolicy({ backoff: { jitter: "equal" } });  // dependency needs a minimum pause (restarting)
new RetryPolicy({ backoff: { jitter: "none" } });   // single script / tests: predictable waits

Equal: lower bound + kuch spread
None: deterministic, debug-friendly
disadvantages: Full: individual wait unpredictable, kabhi ~0
Equal: spread kam
None: fleet mein thundering herd

Jitter ko Retry-After par bhi bina soche lagana

question: Why is the core framework-free, built only on (signal) => Promise, with Express and NestJS as separate entry points?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki failure modes framework ke nahi, dependency ke hain. Ek SMS API Express handler se call ho, NestJS service se, ek BullMQ-type worker se ya cron script se -- timeout, retry, breaker wahi chahiye. PLAN.md decision: "Framework-free core: a policy wraps (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>. That is the shape of fetch(url, { signal }) and of most modern drivers." src/index.ts ka pehla comment: "Core entry point: no framework, no runtime dependency."

Adapters alag entry points hain: package.json exports mein ".", "./express", "./nestjs". Core inme se kuch import nahi karta. Express adapter Express ko bhi import nahi karta -- woh Node ke IncomingMessage / ServerResponse types par likha hai (Express ke req / res unhe extend karte hain). NestJS adapter ko @nestjs/common chahiye, jo OPTIONAL peer dependency hai. PLAN.md: ek package jo dono frameworks import kare, har user par dono thop deta.

Adapters kya karte hain? Teen cheezein: requestSignal (client disconnect -> ClientClosedError se abort hota signal), error mapping (BrokenCircuitError / BulkheadRejectedError -> 503 + Retry-After, TimeoutError -> 504, generic body) aur loadShedding (incoming requests par bulkhead). Matlab framework-specific code sirf "HTTP request ke edges" par hai; resilience logic ek jagah.

Trade-off: core ko AbortSignal ke through cancellation chahiye, toh jo driver signal nahi leta use adapt karna padta hai. Aur adapters ki coverage limited hai -- README honest hai: NestJS sirf platform-express par (Fastify nahi), Express 5 test nahi chala (types same hain, par run nahi kiya), Koa / Hono adapters nahi. npm par publish bhi nahi hai.
why_needed: Business logic aur resilience logic ko framework se tie karna har migration (Express -> Nest, API -> worker) mein rewrite maangta hai. Core alag hone se ek baar test karo, har jagah use karo.
real_world_analogy: Universal power adapter: andar ka charger (core) ek hi hai; plug top (Express, Nest) country ke hisaab se badalta hai. Charger ko plug ke design ka pata nahi.
how_it_works: Core: Policy.execute(op, signal). Adapter request se signal banata hai (requestSignal), use policy.execute ko deta hai, aur jo resilience error bahar aaye use framework ke error path (Express error middleware / Nest ExceptionFilter) mein HTTP response mein badalta hai. mapResilienceError dono adapters share karte hain.

Tests real apps ke against: express.test.ts (Express 4.21.2, 8 tests), nestjs.test.ts (NestJS 10.4.15, 6 tests). README: 179 tests total, Windows, Node 20.

Zero runtime dependencies
Framework upgrade core ko nahi chhoota
disadvantages: Har naye framework ke liye adapter likhna padta hai
Signal-less drivers ko wrap karna padta hai
Adapters ki coverage limited (Fastify / Express 5 / Koa tested nahi)

Policy ko middleware bana dena (phir worker mein use nahi ho sakti)
Har request par nayi policy (state share nahi hoti)

question: Why does RetryPolicy accept injected sleep, random and now functions, and when are fake timers still used?
answer_hinglish:
Retry ka logic time aur randomness par chalta hai -- backoff delay, jitter, deadline. Inhe test karne ke do tareeke hain: global fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers) ya dependency injection. PLAN.md ka decision: "Test hooks instead of global fake time where possible: sleep, random and now can be injected, so retry tests record waits instead of waiting. Fake timers are used where the real timer behaviour is the point."

RetryOptions mein: random?: () => number (default Math.random), sleep?: (ms, signal?) => Promise<void> (default cancellable setTimeout sleep), now?: () => number (default Date.now). CircuitBreaker bhi now leta hai, parseRetryAfter nowMs.

Fayde: test/retry.test.ts ka recorder() sleep ko `async (ms) => void sleeps.push(ms)` bana deta hai -- test turant chalta hai aur exact waits [100, 200] assert karta hai. Deadline test mein now aur sleep dono injected hain: sleep t ko aage badhata hai, toh "virtual time" bina global patching ke. random () => 0.5 se jitter deterministic. budget.test.ts ka 1000-call simulation `sleep: async () => {}` se millisecond mein chalta hai.

Fake timers kab: jab REAL setTimeout behaviour hi test karna ho. "the caller aborts during the wait: rejects at once, no further call (real sleep, fake timers)" -- yahan sleep ka abort + vi.getTimerCount() 0 (timer leak nahi) check karna hai, jo injected fake sleep se prove nahi hota. "the real sleep really waits the backoff" 299 ms par 1 call, 300 par 2. TimeoutPolicy ke tests bhi fake timers use karte hain kyunki unka kaam hi timer hai.

Downside: hooks public options hain, toh production code galti se inhe set kar sakta hai; aur hook-based test real timer ko nahi chhoota, isliye dono types ke tests chahiye.
why_needed: Time-dependent logic ke tests ya toh slow hote hain (real waits) ya flaky (real random). Injection unhe fast aur deterministic banata hai bina global state patch kiye.
real_world_analogy: Flight simulator: pilot training ke liye asli mausam ka intezaar nahi karte, simulator mein "ab toofan" inject karte hain. Par plane ka asli engine test karne ke liye asli engine hi chalana padta hai -- woh fake timers waale tests hain.
how_it_works: execute() shuru mein: const random = o.random ?? Math.random; const sleep = o.sleep ?? realSleep; const now = o.now ?? Date.now; const startedAt = now(). Har jagah yeh local variables use hote hain, globals nahi. Backoff.delayMs(n, random) bhi random parameter leta hai, toh Backoff pure function hai.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts RetryOptions ("Test hooks. Defaults: Math.random, a cancellable setTimeout sleep, Date.now."). test/retry.test.ts: recorder(), "deadline: no retry that would start after it", "uses the default full jitter with the injected random" (waits [50, 100]); fake timers: "the caller aborts during the wait..." aur "the real sleep really waits the backoff (fake timers)". test/budget.test.ts simulate() injected sleep ke saath. test/timeout.test.ts sleep ke tests fake timers se.
advantages: Tests fast aur deterministic
Koi global patching nahi (parallel tests safe)
Simulation (1000 calls) milliseconds mein
disadvantages: Hooks public API ka hissa ban jaate hain
Injected sleep real timer bugs (leak, abort) nahi pakadta -- dono tarah ke tests chahiye
common_mistakes: Sirf injected hooks se test karna aur real sleep ka abort path kabhi test na karna
Fake timers ke baad vi.useRealTimers() na karna (afterEach)
Tests mein Math.random use karna
follow_up_questions: How would you hide test hooks from the public API?
What bugs can fake timers catch that injected sleep cannot?
How do fake timers interact with promises (advanceTimersByTimeAsync)?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Injection explicit hai aur scope-limited (ek policy instance), fake timers global hain par real code path chalate hain. Library dono use karti hai: logic ke liye hooks, timer mechanics ke liye fake timers. Cost: options interface mein teen extra fields jo production mein kabhi set nahi hone chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Test sirf hooks se pass ho aur real sleep abort par timer leak kare -> production mein process exit atke / timers jama. Isi liye mutations R7 (sleep ignores abort) aur R8 (sleep leaves its timer on abort) fake-timer tests pakadte hain. Fake timers ke saath Date.now bhi fake hota hai -- mixed real / fake time se flaky tests.
advanced.alternatives: Clock / Scheduler interface ek object mein (jaise { now, sleep, random }) -- ek hi option. Ya sinon / vitest fake timers har jagah. Ya property-based tests jo random sequences generate karein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Test suite badhne par (179 tests) injected hooks wale tests fast rehte hain; mutation runs (86 breaks, har ek par full suite) tabhi practical hain jab suite fast ho.
advanced.production_improvements: Hooks ko ek alag `testing` options object mein group karna ya internal symbol se expose karna; real-timer integration tests CI mein Linux par bhi chalana (abhi sab results Windows ke hain).

question: When a server's Retry-After is longer than you are willing to wait, why give up instead of parking the request or retrying earlier?
answer_hinglish:
Teen options hain jab server bole "1 ghante baad aana": (a) itna wait karo, (b) apne hisaab se jaldi retry karo, (c) give up. RetryPolicy (c) karti hai jab asked > maxRetryAfterMs (default 60 s), reason "retry-after-too-long", last error unchanged.

(b) kyun nahi: code comment seedha kehta hai -- "Retrying EARLIER than asked would just get another 429." Server ne explicit bataya hai ki woh tab tak accept nahi karega. Jaldi retry = guaranteed fail + server ke rate limiter par extra load + humara budget token waste. Isliye policy kabhi asked se pehle retry nahi karti: final delay hamesha >= asked.

(a) kyun nahi: ek in-memory retry ka wait request ko zinda rakhta hai -- HTTP connection open, upstream user wait kar raha hai, memory mein closure, aur agar bulkhead retry ke bahar ho toh slot bhi. Ek ghanta wait karne waali request ka user kab ka chala gaya. PLAN.md: "gives up instead of parking the request". Aur jo cheez sach mein ek ghante baad karni hai, woh request-response ka kaam hi nahi hai -- woh job queue ka kaam hai.

Toh senior answer: give up fast, aur caller ko honest error do. Agar kaam zaroori hai (jaise SMS bhejna), toh caller us error par job ko durable queue mein schedule kare with delay = Retry-After. Yeh library queue nahi deti; woh scope se bahar hai.

60 s default bhi soch samajh ke: user-facing path mein deadlineMs (jaise README example 8000) pehle trigger hogi; background worker mein 60 s tak wait theek ho sakta hai. Dono knobs alag hain taaki har dependency ke liye tune ho sake.
why_needed: Server ka backpressure respect karna aur apne resources bachana dono zaroori hain. Lambe waits in-memory park karna ek hidden queue hai jisme durability, visibility aur limit kuch nahi.
real_world_analogy: Sarkari office: "saahab 3 baje milenge". 10 minute baad jaake darwaza khatkhatana bekaar (retry earlier). Subah 10 se 3 tak counter par khade rehna bhi bekaar (park). Token lo, ghar jao, 3 baje wapas aao (durable queue).
how_it_works: asked > delayMs hone par hi cap check hota hai: if (asked > (o.maxRetryAfterMs ?? 60_000)) giveUp("retry-after-too-long"). Give up se pehle onGiveUp aur give-up event. Caller ke liye error wahi HttpError hai jisme retryAfterMs field hai -- toh caller use apni queue / response ke liye use kar sakta hai.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts maxRetryAfterMs option aur comment. test/retry.test.ts "Retry-After longer than maxRetryAfterMs: gives up instead of waiting" (asked 3 600 000, cap 60 000, sleeps [], reason retry-after-too-long). Mutation R22 "Retry-After cap ignored" -- ek hi test pakadta hai. Library mein job queue ya durable scheduling NAHI hai.

Server ka rate limit respect
Caller ke paas retryAfterMs info hai to schedule later
disadvantages: User ko error milta hai jahan kabhi wait kar sakte the
Durable retry caller ki zimmedari hai
common_mistakes: Retry-After ko ignore karke apne backoff par retry
Bina cap ke maan lena (request ghanton latki)
Lambe wait ko setTimeout + memory mein 'queue' bana dena

What should your API return to its client in this case?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Latency vs completeness. Give-up user ko jaldi bata deta hai, par kaam drop ho sakta hai agar caller handle na kare. Parking kaam bachata hai par resources aur user ka time khata hai. Senior choice: synchronous path mein give up, important kaam ke liye durable async path.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Process restart ho jaaye jab request park thi -> kaam lost (in-memory). Bahut saari parked requests -> memory / connection exhaustion. Earlier retry -> 429 loop aur rate limiter ki ban-list mein aa jaana.
advanced.alternatives: Durable job queue with delayed jobs (BullMQ-type), client-side token bucket jo outgoing rate ko pehle se limit kare, ya upstream API ka webhook / callback model.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x traffic par ek rate-limited API ke liye per-request retries kaam ke nahi; outgoing calls ko ek central rate limiter / queue se guzarna padta hai. Library ka sab state per-process hai, toh 10 replicas ek shared rate limit ko coordinate nahi karte -- yeh implement nahi hai.

Adapter level par upstream Retry-After ko apne client tak forward karna (abhi sirf breaker / bulkhead ke liye header set hota hai).

question: Walk through RetryPolicy.execute: in what order are the checks made after a failure, and why does the order matter?
answer_hinglish:
execute() ek infinite for loop hai, attempt 1 se. Shuru mein random, sleep, now resolve hote hain (injected ya default) aur startedAt = now().

Har attempt:
1. signal?.throwIfAborted() -- caller pehle se cancel hai toh operation call hi nahi (R26 mutation).
2. operation(signal ?? NEVER). Success -> budget?.onSuccess() aur return.

Failure par catch block, is order mein:
3. signal?.aborted -> throw signal.reason. Caller ne cancel kiya; failure shayad usi cancel ki wajah se hai. Retry nahi, budget nahi chhoona, caller ka reason.
4. shouldRetry false -> giveUp("not-retryable"). Budget se PEHLE, taaki 404 jaise errors token na khayein.
5. budget?.onFailure() -- ek retryable failure dependency ki health ke baare mein info hai, toh token kat-ta hai. Yeh attempts check se PEHLE hai, toh aakhri attempt ki failure bhi gini jaati hai.
6. attempt >= maxAttempts -> giveUp("attempts").
7. budget canRetry() false -> giveUp("budget"). Failing attempt pehle pay karta hai, phir check -- README isko explicitly note karta hai.
8. delayMs = backoff.delayMs(attempt, random); Retry-After bada ho toh woh (ya cap ke upar give up).
9. Deadline: now() + delayMs - startedAt >= deadlineMs -> giveUp("deadline").
10. onRetry callback (`quietly`, throw contained) + retry event (attempt, final delayMs, error).
11. await sleep(delayMs, signal) -- caller wait ke beech abort kare toh turant reject.

Order kyun matter karta hai: agar 3 aur 4 ki jagah badal do, toh caller abort hone par bhi shouldRetry chalega aur budget kat sakta hai (R16 "retries after the caller aborted"). Agar 4 aur 5 badlo, toh non-retryable errors budget drain karenge (R17). Delay ke BAAD deadline check isliye ki asli delay (Retry-After samet) se decide ho.
why_needed: Retry loop ki correctness checks ke order mein hai. Interviewer aksar code walkthrough mangta hai aur yahi edge cases poochta hai.
real_world_analogy: Airport security checklist: pehle "kya passenger ne khud flight cancel ki?", phir "kya ticket valid hai?", phir "seat bachi hai?". Order galat ho toh cancel karne waale ki seat bhi kat jaati hai.
how_it_works: giveUp ek closure hai jo `never` return karta hai (hamesha throw), toh uske baad ka code sirf retry path ke liye hai. Loop condition nahi hai -- exit sirf return ya throw se.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts::RetryPolicy.execute. Har step ke liye test/retry.test.ts mein test hai (22 tests, README), aur README ki mutation list R16-R26 inhi lines ko todti hai: R16 retries after the caller aborted, R17 non-retryable errors drain the budget, R18 one attempt too many, R19 budget not checked, R20 success not reported to the budget, R21 Retry-After ignored, R23 deadline ignored, R24 backoff wait not cancellable, R25 wrapper instead of last error, R26 already-aborted caller.

Give-up reasons distinct aur observable
Caller abort sabse pehle -- koi wasted kaam nahi

question: Walk through TimeoutPolicy.execute line by line: why the 'stopped' promise, the async wrapper and the finally block?
answer_hinglish:
Code chhota hai par har line ek bug rokti hai.

1. signal?.throwIfAborted() -- caller already aborted toh operation call nahi (R6).
2. const controller = new AbortController() -- har call ka apna controller; operation ko controller.signal milta hai, caller ka signal nahi. Isi se timeout operation ko abort kar sakta hai bina caller ke signal ko chhue.
3. onCallerAbort listener ({ once: true }) -- caller ka abort controller tak (R4).
4. setTimeout: timeout event emit, phir controller.abort(new TimeoutError(ms)) (R1 reason ke saath).
5. `stopped` promise: controller.signal ke abort par controller.signal.reason se reject. Ek hi promise dono cases cover karta hai -- timeout aur caller abort -- "for whichever reason". Isse execute() turant reject hota hai chahe operation signal ignore kare (R5).
6. Promise.race([(async () => operation(controller.signal))(), stopped]). Async IIFE kyun: agar operation SYNCHRONOUSLY throw kare (async function nahi, normal function jo throw kare), toh direct operation(...) call array banate waqt hi throw kar deta, race shuru hone se pehle. Code comment ke words mein wrapper ke saath "an operation that throws synchronously becomes a rejection like any other failure" -- ek hi path, koi special case nahi (test "passes the operation's own error through" "sync boom" bhi check karta hai).
7. finally: clearTimeout(timer) (R2) aur removeEventListener (R3). Success, failure, timeout -- har path par cleanup.

Subtle point: haarne waale promise ki late rejection race ne already handle ki hoti hai, toh unhandled rejection nahi; aur operation pehle khatam ho toh `stopped` kabhi settle nahi hota, bas garbage collect ho jaata hai.

Benchmark note: yahi per-call AbortController + timer + listeners timeout ko sabse mehenga policy banata hai -- README: 7745 / 8194 ns per call (two runs) vs ~131-146 ns bare call, Windows 11, Ryzen 5 4500, Node 20.20.1; cockatiel ka timeout 30413 / 31551 ns.
why_needed: Timeout implementation mein leaks (timers, listeners), sync throws aur unhandled rejections common bugs hain. Line-by-line samajhna interviewer ko dikhata hai ki aap edge cases jaante ho.
real_world_analogy: Race ka referee: do runners (operation aur stopwatch). Jo pehle pahunche woh jeeta; doosra baad mein aaye toh bhi uska result discard -- par race khatam hone par referee stopwatch band karta hai aur barrier hata deta hai (finally).
how_it_works: Promise.race har input promise par handlers attach karta hai, toh haarne waale ki rejection bhi "handled" hai. AbortController.abort() pehli baar hi event fire karta hai; baad ke abort calls no-op hain, toh timeout aur caller abort ek saath aaye toh pehla reason jeet-ta hai.

Overhead numbers bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-run1.json aur run2.json se (medianNsPerCall "ours: timeout" 7745.4 aur 8194).

Har path par cleanup
Sync throw bhi normal rejection
disadvantages: Per call AbortController + timer + 2-3 listeners -- measured sabse mehenga hissa
Operation ignore kare toh kaam background mein chalta hai
common_mistakes: finally ke bina clearTimeout sirf success path par
Operation ko caller ka signal dena (timeout use abort nahi kar sakta)
Race mein haarne waale promise ki rejection ko unhandled samajhna / swallow karne ke liye extra catch

Ek shared timer wheel / AbortSignal.timeout se cost kam ho sakti thi, par caller-link aur custom TimeoutError reason ke saath complexity badhti. Benchmark kehta hai ours cockatiel se ~4x sasta tha in runs, par WHY investigate nahi hua (README).

question: How does the cancellable sleep in src/sleep.ts work, and what would break if the backoff wait were a plain setTimeout?
answer_hinglish:
src/sleep.ts ek chhota function hai: sleep(ms, signal?) jo ek Promise return karta hai. File ka pehla comment hi reason hai: "Without this, a cancelled request would still sit out its backoff delay."

Kaam kaise karta hai:
1. Signal pehle se aborted -> turant reject(signal.reason), koi timer nahi banta.
2. onAbort handler: clearTimeout(timer) aur reject(signal.reason).
3. setTimeout(ms): fire hone par signal se onAbort listener hatata hai aur resolve.
4. signal par onAbort listener { once: true }.

Toh do exits hain aur dono saaf: time poora hua -> listener removed, resolve. Abort hua -> timer cleared, reject caller ke reason se. Koi timer peeche nahi bachta, koi listener nahi.

Plain setTimeout (new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))) se kya tootta: maan lo backoff 10 s ka hai aur client ne 1 s par connection band kar diya. Retry policy 9 s aur sota rehta, phir check karta (throwIfAborted loop ke top par) aur tab rukta. Tab tak request ki memory, closures, aur agar bulkhead retry ke bahar ho toh slot bhi pakda rehta. Aur ek pending timer process ko graceful shutdown par zinda rakhta hai.

Tests: "rejects at once with the abort reason, and leaves no timer behind" (fake timers, vi.getTimerCount() 0), "rejects without waiting if already aborted", aur retry level par "the caller aborts during the wait: rejects at once, no further call (real sleep, fake timers)" -- 10 s backoff ke 5 s par abort, f.calls() 1. Mutations R7 (sleep ignores abort), R8 (sleep leaves its timer on abort) aur R24 (backoff wait not cancellable) sab pakde gaye.

sleep index.ts se export bhi hota hai, toh apne code mein bhi cancellable wait ke liye use kar sakte ho.
why_needed: PLAN.md: caller ka signal "should stop the work, the retries and the backoff wait at once". Backoff wait retry ka sabse lamba hissa ho sakta hai -- wahi cancellable na ho toh cancellation adhoori hai.
real_world_analogy: Alarm laga ke so gaye, par beech mein phone aaya ki meeting cancel -- aap uthke alarm band karte ho (clearTimeout), alarm bajne tak sote nahi rehte.
how_it_works: Promise executor mein synchronously signal check, phir timer aur listener. `timer` const onAbort se pehle declare nahi hai par onAbort sirf baad mein (abort par) chalta hai, tab tak timer assign ho chuka hota hai -- closure order safe hai.
in_this_project: src/sleep.ts::sleep; RetryPolicy ka default sleep yahi hai (import { sleep as realSleep }). test/timeout.test.ts ke "sleep" describe block mein 3 tests; test/retry.test.ts ka fake-timer abort test.

Koi timer / listener leak nahi
Reusable (exported)
disadvantages: Node ke timers/promises setTimeout(ms, undefined, { signal }) se thoda zyada code
Har call ek listener add / remove
common_mistakes: Timer fire hone par listener na hatana (long-lived signal par leak)
Abort par clearTimeout bhool jaana
Already-aborted signal ke liye timer bana dena
follow_up_questions: How does Node's timers/promises setTimeout with a signal compare?
Why does the timer path remove the listener but the abort path does not need to?
How would you test that no timer is left behind?

question: Walk through the code that turns a fetch response into a retry decision: HttpError, parseRetryAfter and isRetryableHttp together.
answer_hinglish:
Library fetch ko khud call nahi karti -- operation aapka hai. Pattern README aur test/http.test.ts ka getJson() helper dikhata hai:

1. fetch(url, { signal }) -- policy ka signal pass, taaki timeout / caller abort connection tod sake.
2. !res.ok par: body cancel (await res.body?.cancel() -- warna connection / stream latka reh sakta hai), phir throw new HttpError(res.status, parseRetryAfter(res.headers.get("retry-after"))).
3. ok par res.json().

HttpError(upstreamStatus, retryAfterMs) do readonly fields carry karta hai. Message "upstream answered HTTP 503". Field ka naam `upstreamStatus` jaan-boojh kar hai: Express ka default error handler err.status client ko bhejta hai; `status` hota toh dependency ka 404 HAMARA 404 ban jaata (H1 mutation, 3 tests).

Phir RetryPolicy:
- shouldRetry: isRetryableHttp -> 503 / 429 / 408 / network error / TimeoutError retry; 404 etc. nahi; breaker / bulkhead rejections nahi.
- retryAfterMs: (e) => (e instanceof HttpError ? e.retryAfterMs : undefined) -> server ka maanga delay policy tak.

Toh decision teen chhote pure pieces se banta hai: parse (header -> ms), classify (error -> retryable?), aur policy (kitna wait / give up). Har piece alag test hota hai: parseRetryAfter ke table-driven cases, isRetryableHttp ke 14 cases, aur phir end-to-end real server par: "503, 503, 200: the third request succeeds" (3 hits), "404 is not retried" (1 hit), "429 with Retry-After: 1" (wait 1000), "all attempts 503: the last HttpError comes back unchanged".

Ek note: res.status 2xx ke alawa sab HttpError ban jaata hai -- 3xx bhi agar fetch redirect follow na kare. Yeh caller ka helper hai, library ka nahi; aap apni zaroorat ke hisaab se badal sakte ho.
why_needed: Retry decision ka data (status, Retry-After) response mein hai, policy ko error object mein milta hai. Iska saaf mapping na ho toh policy andhi hai.
real_world_analogy: Hospital triage: reception (getJson) patient ki report (status, Retry-After) ek file (HttpError) mein daalta hai; doctor (RetryPolicy) file padh ke decide karta hai ki "kal aana" ya "ghar jao".
how_it_works: HttpError extends Error, `override name = "HttpError"` taaki logs / toMatchObject({ name }) mein dikhe. retryAfterMs undefined ho sakta hai. isRetryableHttp sirf upstreamStatus padhta hai; Retry-After ka use RetryPolicy karti hai.

upstreamStatus se framework galti se client ko status nahi bhejta

Signal fetch ko pass na karna
