question: Coding exercise: implement a decorrelated-jitter Backoff that plugs into RetryPolicy, and write a test for it.
answer_hinglish:
RetryPolicy custom backoff leti hai: koi bhi object jiske paas delayMs(retryNumber, random) ho (constructor mein `"delayMs" in b` check). Decorrelated jitter (AWS article ka teesra variant) ka formula: sleep = min(cap, random_between(base, prev x 3)), jahan prev pichhla sleep hai aur shuru mein base.

Trap yahan hai, aur interviewer yahi dekhna chahega: decorrelated jitter ko PICHHLA delay chahiye, matlab state. Lekin ek RetryPolicy (aur uska Backoff object) per dependency EK BAAR banta hai aur saari concurrent calls share karti hain (README: "created once, shared by every call"). Agar Backoff object mein `prev` field rakha, toh call A ka prev call B ke delay ko affect karega -- concurrent requests ek doosre ki state bigaad denge. retryNumber === 1 par reset karna bhi kaam nahi karta jab do calls interleave hon.

Solution: stateless rakho. delayMs ko sirf retryNumber aur random milta hai, toh hum chain ko har baar 1 se n tak replay karte hain: prev = base; har step par prev = min(cap, base + random() x (prev x 3 - base)). n-th value ka distribution exactly decorrelated jitter ke n-th step jaisa hai; fark sirf yeh ki yeh actual pichhle sleep se correlated nahi (har call fresh random draws leta hai). Cost O(n) random draws -- n maxAttempts se bada nahi hota, toh negligible. Concurrency-safe aur pure, toh injected random se deterministic test.

Validation existing exponentialBackoff jaisa: baseMs >= 0, capMs >= baseMs, warna RangeError. Test mein random () => 0.5 ke saath sequence haath se nikala ja sakta hai: base 100, cap 1000 -> 200, 350, 575, 912, 1000. Aur RetryPolicy integration: flaky(2) ke saath sleeps [200, 350].
why_needed: Library ka Backoff interface extension point hai; real teams apni strategy chahti hain. Exercise interface ki ek hidden constraint (shared, concurrent use = stateless) samajhna sikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi recipe card poore restaurant ke chefs share karte hain. Card par "pichhli baar kitna namak daala" likhoge toh har chef doosre ka likha padhega. Recipe aisi likho jo sirf "kaunsa step" se kaam kare.
how_it_works: delayMs(n, random): prev = base; for i in 1..n: prev = min(cap, base + random() * (prev * 3 - base)); return floor(prev). r = 0 hamesha base deta hai; r ~ 1 se prev har step ~3x, cap tak. Integer output (Math.floor) existing backoff jaisa.
in_this_project: Yeh file repo mein NAHI hai -- exercise hai. Interface src/backoff.ts::Backoff hai; RetryPolicy constructor custom object accept karta hai (test/retry.test.ts "accepts a custom Backoff object": { delayMs: (n) => n * 7 } se sleeps [7, 14]). Test pattern wahi recorder-style: injected random aur sleep.
advantages: Concurrency-safe (no shared mutable state)
Existing extension point use, RetryPolicy unchanged
Injected random se deterministic test
disadvantages: Actual pichhle sleep se correlate nahi (approximation of the 'true' stateful version)
O(n) random draws per delay
common_mistakes: Backoff object mein `prev` field rakhna (concurrent calls ki state mix)
Cap har step par na lagana (overflow / huge waits)
Test mein Math.random se exact values expect karna
follow_up_questions: How would you make the Backoff stateful per call without changing RetryPolicy?
How does decorrelated jitter compare to full jitter in total load?
What property-based test would you add?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Stateless replay vs true correlation. Exact AWS variant ke liye per-call state chahiye, jo current interface (delayMs(n, random)) nahi deta; interface badalna (jaise createSession()) API change hai. Replay version interface ke andar rehke same marginal distribution deta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Stateful version + concurrent calls -> delays unpredictable, ek call doosre ke chain ko reset kar de. Cap na lagao -> prev x 3 kuch hi steps mein huge. random 1.0 return kare (contract [0,1) todta hua) -> cap se clamp ho jaata hai, theek.
advanced.alternatives: Per-call state ke liye Backoff interface mein ek factory method (start(): (n) => number) add karna; ya RetryPolicy ke execute ke andar prev delay pass karna (delayMs(n, random, prevDelay)) -- dono library ke API changes hain jo abhi nahi hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x clients par decorrelated aur full jitter dono load spread karte hain; asli limit volume hai, jo RetryBudget aur breaker sambhalte hain. O(n) draws n <= maxAttempts (default 3) par irrelevant.
advanced.production_improvements: Backoff strategies ko exponentialBackoff ke saath backoff.ts mein ek option banana (jitter: "decorrelated"), retry delay histogram metric, aur property-based tests (fast-check type) jo har random sequence par range check karein.

question: Coding exercise: write a shouldRetry predicate for a PostgreSQL driver's error codes and test it with RetryPolicy.
answer_hinglish:
RetryPolicy ka shouldRetry(error, attempt) koi bhi predicate le sakta hai; isRetryableHttp sirf HTTP ke liye hai. Database ke liye retryable ka matlab alag hai. Postgres errors par SQLSTATE `code` hota hai (5 character, jaise "40001"), aur Node ke network errors par `code` jaise "ECONNRESET". (Repo mein koi DB driver nahi hai -- yeh exercise hai; codes PostgreSQL docs ke standard SQLSTATE hain.)

Retryable (dobara try karne par badal sakta hai):
- 40001 serialization_failure, 40P01 deadlock_detected -- concurrency conflict; dobara chalane par aksar pass.
- 08xxx connection exceptions (08000, 08003, 08006, 08001), 57P01 admin_shutdown, 53300 too_many_connections -- server / connection side transient.
- Node network codes: ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE.
- TimeoutError (hamari TimeoutPolicy) -- PAR sirf idempotent operation ke liye.

Non-retryable: 23505 unique_violation, 23503 foreign_key_violation, 42601 syntax_error, 42P01 undefined_table, 22xxx data exceptions -- same query same jawab dega. Aur BrokenCircuitError / BulkheadRejectedError hamesha false (isRetryableHttp jaisa reason: fail fast).

Do important design points:
1. Idempotency: write query timeout hui toh shayad commit ho chuka ho. Isliye predicate factory `{ idempotent }` leti hai; non-idempotent ke liye TimeoutError aur ambiguous connection loss (08006 / ECONNRESET beech mein) retry nahi.
2. 40001 / 40P01 ka retry tabhi sahi hai jab Operation POORA transaction ho (BEGIN ... COMMIT), sirf failed statement nahi -- Postgres transaction abort kar chuka hota hai.

Test: predicate ke unit cases + RetryPolicy ke saath ek flaky operation jo pehle 40001 throw kare phir succeed, aur ek jo 23505 throw kare aur ek hi call ke baad give up "not-retryable".
why_needed: Generic "retry everything" DB par duplicate inserts ya bekaar retries (syntax errors) karta hai; error codes ki samajh se hi safe retry hota hai.
real_world_analogy: ATM: "server busy, phir try karo" (40001 / 08006) vs "account number galat" (23503) vs "transaction hua ya nahi pata nahi" (timeout) -- teesre case mein bina check kiye dobara paisa nahi bhejte.
how_it_works: Predicate pehle resilience rejections reject karta hai, phir TimeoutError (idempotency par depend), phir error.code string dekhta hai: exact set ya prefix (class "08"). Unknown errors ke liye conservative default: false (DB ke liye "jo nahi jaante use retry mat karo").
in_this_project: Yeh predicate repo mein NAHI hai. Pattern src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp jaisa hai (resilience rejections pehle false). RetryPolicy ka shouldRetry contract aur give-up reason "not-retryable" src/retry.ts mein hai; test style test/retry.test.ts jaisa (injected sleep).
advantages: Sirf woh errors retry jo badal sakte hain
Idempotency explicit, galti se duplicate write nahi
RetryPolicy unchanged, sirf predicate
disadvantages: Driver-specific codes maintain karne padte hain
Unknown errors ko false maanna kabhi genuine transient error miss karta hai
common_mistakes: 40001 par sirf failed statement retry karna (poora transaction chahiye)
Write timeout ko blindly retry (duplicate insert / double charge)
Unique violation retry karna
follow_up_questions: How would you make a write idempotent so it can be retried safely?
Why must the whole transaction be the Operation for 40001?
Should the circuit breaker's isFailure use the same predicate?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Conservative (unknown = no retry) vs aggressive (unknown = retry, jaise isRetryableHttp non-HTTP errors ke liye karta hai). DB writes ke liye conservative better hai kyunki galat retry ka cost (duplicate data) galat give-up (ek error user ko) se zyada hai. Breaker ke isFailure ke liye alag predicate chahiye: 40001 dependency down nahi hai, contention hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ambiguous failure (commit ke baad connection toota) par non-idempotent retry -> duplicate row / double charge. 40001 storm: high contention par sab retry karein toh contention aur badhti hai -- budget aur jitter yahan zaroori. Pool exhausted (53300) par retry -> aur connections maangna.
advanced.alternatives: Idempotency keys / upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) taaki writes safely retryable hon; driver ki built-in retry (kuch ORMs transaction retry dete hain); outbox pattern jahan side effects ek hi transaction mein record hon.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x load par serialization failures badhte hain (zyada concurrent transactions). Retry tab sirf symptom chhupata hai; isolation level / schema / hot-row contention fix karni padti hai. Library ka budget per-process hai, toh 50 replicas ka combined retry load bound nahi hota.
advanced.production_improvements: SQLSTATE ke hisaab se retry metrics (retry event ka error.code label), 40001 rate par alert, transaction-level retry helper jo BEGIN / COMMIT ko Operation mein wrap kare, aur driver ke signal support ke saath TimeoutPolicy (query cancel).

question: Your dependency is slow, not down. Walk through what this library's timeout and retry do in that case, and where they can make things worse.
answer_hinglish:
Slow dependency sabse tricky case hai, kyunki woh "fail" nahi hoti -- bas p99 badh jaata hai. Maan lo SMS API normally 200 ms leti hai, ab 2.5 s le rahi hai, aur README example jaisa setup hai: TimeoutPolicy 2000 ms per attempt, RetryPolicy maxAttempts 3, deadlineMs 8000.

Kya hota hai: har attempt 2 s par TimeoutError, signal abort hota hai (fetch connection todta hai, toh dependency ko bhi request cancel dikhti hai). isRetryableHttp TimeoutError ko retryable maanta hai, toh retry -- aur kyunki dependency slow hai, agla attempt bhi timeout. Result: har request 3 attempts, 6+ s, aur fail. Dependency par load 3x ho gaya jab woh pehle se struggle kar rahi thi -- yeh retry amplification hai, aur slow hone ki wajah agar load hi hai toh yeh positive feedback loop hai.

Kya bachata hai (library mein jo hai):
- Timeout ka abort: zombie requests nahi, toh dependency par load sirf "naye attempts" ka hai, purane piled-up nahi.
- deadlineMs: total time bound; retry jo deadline ke baad start ho woh nahi hota.
- RetryBudget: sustained failures par retries band -- README simulation mein 1000 calls ke 3000 attempts budget ke saath 1003 ho jaate hain.
- Jitter: retries ek saath nahi aate.

Kahan galat ho sakta hai: timeout p99 se tight ho toh normal slow requests bhi kat-ti hain aur retries load badhate hain. Har layer khud retry kare toh 3 x 3 x 3 = 27x (budget.ts comment). Breaker "slow call rate" nahi jaanta (README NOT implemented) -- slow calls tabhi failure hain jab timeout breaker ke andar ho. Deadline propagation, adaptive concurrency, hedging -- implement nahi.

Senior answer: timeout ko dependency ke healthy p99 ke upar set karo, retries sirf ek layer par, budget hamesha on, timeout breaker ke andar.
why_needed: Outages aksar "slow" se shuru hote hain, "down" se nahi. Galat tuned timeout + retry ek slow dependency ko down dependency bana dete hain.
real_world_analogy: Traffic jam mein har gaadi ek alag route try kare (retry) toh doosri sadak bhi jam. Kuch gaadiyan ruk jaayein (budget) aur purani gaadiyan raste se hat jaayein (abort) tabhi jam khulta hai.
how_it_works: Timeline per call: attempt 1 (0-2 s) timeout -> backoff ~0-100 ms (full jitter) -> attempt 2 (timeout) -> backoff ~0-200 ms -> attempt 3 -> give up "attempts". Budget: har timeout ek token (retryable error); 10 tokens se 5 ke neeche jaate hi har call sirf ek attempt. Deadline 8000 ms isme hit nahi hoti (~6.3 s max), toh yahan bound attempts kar rahe hain.
in_this_project: src/timeout.ts (abort), src/retry.ts (deadlineMs, budget), src/http.ts (isRetryableHttp: TimeoutError true), src/budget.ts comment "3 x 3 x 3 = 27x". README "NOT implemented": count-based window only, no slow-call rate; nothing shared between processes; hedged requests, adaptive concurrency not built. test/http.test.ts "hang, hang, 200: each attempt times out on its own and the third succeeds".
advantages: Abort se zombie load nahi
Budget sustained slowness mein retries band karta hai
Deadline total latency bound karti hai
disadvantages: Retry slow dependency par load badhata hai
Tight timeout normal slow requests bhi kaat-ta hai
Slow-call detection breaker mein nahi (timeout ke through hi)
common_mistakes: Timeout ko average latency par set karna (p99 nahi)
Har layer par retries
Budget ke bina retry
follow_up_questions: How do you choose a timeout from latency percentiles?
What is hedging and why is it not here?
How would adaptive concurrency limits help a slow dependency?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Availability vs load. Retry ek request ki success chance badhata hai par aggregate load bhi; budget yeh trade-off bound karta hai (~10% extra in steady state, gRPC throttling ki tarah). Tight timeout latency bachata hai par false failures + retries badhata hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Retry storm slow dependency par -> woh fully down. Timeout dependency ke p99 se kam -> healthy state mein bhi retries. Saare replicas ka apna budget -> combined retries replicas x local budget (shared nahi). Operation signal ignore kare -> abort ke baad bhi requests chalti, load piled up.
advanced.alternatives: Hedged requests (p95 par doosri request, pehli jeete) -- tail latency ke liye, par load badhata hai; not implemented. Adaptive concurrency (TCP-Vegas / gradient type limiters) -- not implemented. Service mesh outlier detection. Deadline propagation (gRPC deadlines) -- not implemented.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x RPS par 3x retry amplification absolute numbers mein bahut bada; budget ke bina 100x par dependency ka recover hona mushkil. Per-process state matlab 100 replicas = 100 alag budgets aur breakers; har ek ko khud seekhna padta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Latency histograms se timeout tune karna, retry / give-up / timeout events par metrics (onEvent ready hai), retries sirf ek layer par (edge par nahi), aur load test jo slow (not down) dependency simulate kare -- yeh project mein nahi hai.

question: How would you use this library to call a non-idempotent dependency, such as sending an SMS or charging a card, without causing duplicates?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: library khud idempotency nahi deti; woh sirf decide karti hai KAB dobara call karna. Duplicate se bachna caller aur dependency ke contract ka kaam hai. Isliye non-idempotent call par retry policy configure karte waqt "kaunsa failure ambiguous hai" sochna zaroori hai.

Failures ke teen type:
1. Request pahunchi hi nahi -- ECONNREFUSED, ya open breaker / full bulkhead (operation call hi nahi hua). Retry safe.
2. Server ne clearly mana kiya -- 429, 503 jo request process karne se pehle aaya (Retry-After ke saath). Aam taur par safe, agar API document karta hai ki 503 par kuch nahi hua.
3. Ambiguous -- TimeoutError (hamara 2 s ka timeout fire hua, par server ne shayad SMS bhej diya), connection reset beech mein, 500 / 502 / 504. Yahan blind retry = do SMS / do charges.

isRetryableHttp category 3 ko retryable maanta hai (TimeoutError aur 5xx true) -- yeh idempotent calls ke liye sahi default hai, par payment ke liye nahi. Toh do options:
(a) Idempotency key: har logical operation ke liye ek key (UUID) ek baar banao, Operation ke BAHAR, aur har attempt mein same key header bhejo. Server same key par dobara kaam nahi karta. Tab poora isRetryableHttp safe hai. Bahut payment APIs yahi support karte hain.
(b) Agar dependency key support nahi karti: shouldRetry custom -- sirf category 1 aur 2, TimeoutError aur 5xx nahi. Ambiguous failure par caller ko "unknown" status do aur baad mein reconcile karo.

Key Operation ke andar banaoge toh har attempt naya key -- poora point khatam. Yeh sabse common bug hai.

Library ka hissa: shouldRetry hook, last error unchanged (caller ko TimeoutError dikhe toh woh "unknown" handle kare), events for audit. Idempotency store, reconciliation -- implement nahi.
why_needed: Payments, SMS, emails mein duplicate ka cost user-visible aur kabhi financial hai. Retry library ko "safe" maan lena sabse mehenga galti hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko parcel diya aur receipt nahi mili. Dobara parcel bhejoge toh customer ko do mil sakte hain. Tracking number (idempotency key) ho toh courier khud bata deta hai "yeh pehle hi aa chuka hai".
how_it_works: Key generation execute() se pehle: const key = randomUUID(); sms.execute((s) => fetch(url, { headers: { "idempotency-key": key }, signal: s })). RetryPolicy har attempt mein same closure chalati hai, toh same key. TimeoutPolicy abort request ko client side par todta hai, par server ne process kar liya ho sakta hai -- abort "undo" nahi hai.
in_this_project: src/retry.ts shouldRetry hook aur last-error-unchanged rule; src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp (TimeoutError aur 5xx retryable -- idempotency-agnostic); src/timeout.ts abort sirf client side cancel hai. Idempotency keys, dedup store, reconciliation is library mein NAHI hain.

shouldRetry se ambiguous failures exclude
Last error unchanged: caller TimeoutError ko 'unknown' maan sakta hai
disadvantages: Dependency ko key support karna chahiye
Bina key ke kuch genuine transient failures retry nahi hote
Reconciliation ka kaam caller par
common_mistakes: Key ko Operation ke andar generate karna
isRetryableHttp ko payment par as-is use karna
Timeout abort ko 'request cancel ho gayi server par bhi' samajhna

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Availability vs exactly-once effect. Aggressive retry success rate badhata hai par duplicates ka risk; conservative retry duplicates se bachata hai par user ko zyada errors. Idempotency key yeh trade-off tod deta hai, par dependency side par storage aur contract chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Timeout ke baad retry, dependency ne pehla process kar liya -> do SMS / do charges. Key har attempt nayi -> wahi problem. Key store expire ho gaya retry se pehle -> duplicate. Process crash retry ke beech -> caller ko pata nahi kya hua (reconciliation chahiye).
advanced.alternatives: Outbox pattern + async worker jo ek hi baar bhejta hai; dependency ka status / lookup API se pehle check karna ki operation hua ya nahi; at-least-once + dedup on receiver side.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x traffic par duplicate rate (ambiguous failures ka % x volume) absolute numbers mein bada hota hai; idempotency key store ki throughput aur TTL design karna padta hai. Library ka state in-process hai; idempotency state hamesha dependency / DB mein hona chahiye, memory mein nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Unknown-outcome errors ke liye explicit type / metric, give-up events ke saath idempotency key log karna (audit), reconciliation job jo dependency se status match kare, aur per-dependency documented shouldRetry (reads ke liye isRetryableHttp, writes ke liye conservative).
